desc:
Order fraud review and payment checks help you decide which orders to ship, hold or question. Ecom Swift LLC reviews flagged orders, failed payments and disputes in your own store, then gives you clear rules your team can follow.

## What is an order fraud review?

An order fraud review is a manual check of orders that look risky before they leave your warehouse. A reviewer compares the facts of the order against what a genuine purchase usually looks like, then recommends ship, hold or contact the customer.

Automatic risk tools in your store give a first signal. They cannot know your customers, your products or your normal patterns. A person reading the order in context fills that gap.

## Why one bad order can cost more than a good one earns

When a fraudulent order ships, you lose the goods and the shipping cost, and you may also face a dispute and its fees. Repeated disputes can put pressure on your relationship with your payment provider. The cost lands on one order but the damage reaches your whole account.

The opposite mistake is also costly. Cancelling a real customer's order because it looked odd loses a sale and may lose the customer. A good review sits between the two: it holds what is truly doubtful and releases what is fine.

## How payment checks protect profit

Fraud review works by adding friction in the right place. Most risk signals are individually weak: a new customer, a rush shipping choice, a large basket. The signal becomes useful when several appear together, such as a billing address far from the shipping address, a high-value order of resalable goods and a free email domain.

Checking failed payments helps too. A run of declined cards on one order, followed by a success, is a common pattern. Looking at disputes shows which products and routes attract trouble, so you can respond to causes and not only to individual cases.

## What a careful review includes

- The risk analysis your platform or fraud app shows for each flagged order.
- A comparison of billing and shipping addresses.
- The order's size, items and shipping speed against the customer's history.
- How the payment was made and whether earlier attempts failed.
- Checks on email, phone and delivery address for obvious problems.
- A clear decision with short notes: ship, hold or contact.
- A customer verification message that is polite and brief.
- A list of warning signs written for your team.
- A pattern report across reviewed orders.

## What we do

We work in your store admin with limited staff access. For each flagged order, we gather the facts, apply a consistent checklist and write a short note with our recommendation. Where we are unsure, we draft a message asking the customer to confirm a detail, so a genuine buyer can clear the hold quickly.

Where your platform supports order risk rules or a fraud app, we check how they are set and suggest changes. In the Standard and Premium packages we also review failed payments and disputes, and we prepare an evidence template for disputes. We do not need access to your payment provider account to do this work, because the order and payment status we need appear in your store.

We cannot catch every fraudulent order, and no review can. Our aim is to give you more facts and a repeatable method.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Hold shipments until an unclear order is confirmed.
- Keep proof of delivery for higher-value orders.
- Write down the decisions you make, so patterns appear.
- Ask a customer a polite question before assuming bad intent.
- Review your settings after any dispute.

**Avoid:**
- Cancelling an order only because the customer is new.
- Shipping to a changed address without checking it.
- Ignoring failed payment attempts.
- Sending accusing or harsh messages to customers.
- Relying on one risk score alone.

## Who this is for

This suits a store that has recently suffered a chargeback and wants to understand it. It suits a seller of high-resale products, such as electronics or limited-edition items, who needs a second pair of eyes before dispatch. It also suits an owner who is nervous about a sale peak, when fraud attempts tend to hide among genuine orders.

## What we need from you

Tell us how many orders are flagged, how fast you ship and what level of risk you accept. Add us as a staff or collaborator user with permission to view orders. We never need passwords or card details. Send us any past disputes you want us to learn from, and we will reply with a plan and a short list of questions.
